summary: This bill eliminates the 400 percent income limit on eligibility for the refundable premium tax credit for health insurance and updates the sliding scale so households pay between 0 and 8.5 percent of income toward premiums based on income level as a percentage of the poverty line, effective for tax years after 2025.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to expand eligibility for the refundable premium tax credit under section 36B by removing the 400% of poverty line income cap and adjusting premium percentages up to 8.5% for incomes 400% and higher. Refundable tax credits represent direct government expenditures, as they provide payments even if no taxes are owed. This expansion significantly increases federal spending on healthcare subsidies by making the credit available to higher-income households, directly pushing toward expanded government spending.

The bill expands a refundable tax credit for health insurance premiums, which reduces the effective tax burden for eligible households by providing larger credits or refunds, particularly for those above 400% of poverty. This functions as a tax cut or revenue reduction without raising rates elsewhere, aligning with lower taxes.

The bill primarily enhances affordability of private qualified health plans through expanded federal premium tax credits under the ACA marketplaces, removing income limits and capping contributions. This promotes broader access to subsidized private coverage, moving toward greater public support for healthcare access without shifting to single-payer, but strongly favoring subsidized private/market-based systems over pure market.

This directly increases federal outlays on a refundable tax credit, pushing the bill toward accepting larger deficits to fund expanded health coverage.
